claim: IAEval's format is full papers up to 9 pages or short papers up to 4 pages excluding references/appendices, official NeurIPS 2026 style/Overleaf template, double-blind review with explicit anonymization instructions, non-archival, and work under review at or already accepted to other venues is explicitly welcome.
stance_target: Page limit, anonymity, and archival status of IAEval
scope_conditions: Call for papers, Format and length, Double-blind review, Non-archival
quoted_support: Full papers may be up to 9 pages and short papers up to 4 pages, excluding references and appendices. ... All submissions are reviewed double-blind... The workshop is non-archival and accepted papers will not appear in published proceedings. You may submit work that is currently under review at, or has already been accepted to, another venue.

claim: IAEval scope centers on evaluation methodology for multi-turn/tool-using/interactive LLM agents -- trajectory-level evaluation, user-simulator validation, and grader design -- and states 'early-stage work is welcome,' but has no explicit statement on negative results specifically.
stance_target: Topical fit and stated openness to early-stage/negative findings at IAEval
scope_conditions: Why this workshop, Call for papers
quoted_support: We invite submissions on the topics listed above. Early-stage work is welcome.

claim: IAEval has a distinctive 'opinion papers' track requiring the title format 'Opinion: [Your Title]', a lower-barrier submission type for argumentative/critical contributions.
quoted_support: We welcome opinion papers. The title must state the opinion and follow the format "Opinion: [Your Title]" — for example, "Opinion: Large Language Models Should Not Replace Peer Review in Scientific Publishing".
